name: Question 10
problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=t-2{t}^{4}$, where $t\ge 0$ is the time. If the particle has position $x=\frac{1}{10}$ and velocity $v=\frac{1}{10}$ when $t=1$, calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t>0.$
worked_solution:
We start by integrating the acceleration to get the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (t-2{t}^{4})\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}-\frac{2}{5}{t}^{5}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)=\frac{1}{10}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{10} & =\frac{1}{2}(1)^{2}-\frac{2}{5}(1)^{5}+C \\ \frac{1}{10} & =\frac{1}{2}-\frac{2}{5}+C \\ C & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So the velocity is given by $v(t)=\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}-\frac{2}{5}{t}^{5}.$ 

Now, we integrate the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}-\frac{2}{5}{t}^{5})\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{t}^{3}-\frac{1}{15}{t}^{6}+K\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $K$, we use the fact that $x(1)=\frac{1}{10}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{10} & =\frac{1}{6}(1)^{3}-\frac{1}{15}(1)^{6}+K \\ \frac{1}{10} & =\frac{1}{6}-\frac{1}{15}+K \\ \frac{1}{10} & =\frac{1}{10}+K \\ K & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)=\frac{1}{6}{t}^{3}-\frac{1}{15}{t}^{6}.
$$

Question 10
?

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration a(t)=t−2t4, where t≥0 is the time. If the particle has position x=110 and velocity v=110 when t=1, calculate the position x of the particle at time t>0.

a
x(t)=13t3−112t6
b
x(t)=16t3−115t6+120t2
c
x(t)=16t3
d
x(t)=16t3−115t6+120t2
e
x(t)=16t3−115t6
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We start by integrating the acceleration to get the velocity v(t):

v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫(t−2t4)dt=12t2−25t5+C

To determine C, we use the fact that v(1)=110. Substituting this into the above gives

110=12(1)2−25(1)5+C110=12−25+CC=0.

So the velocity is given by v(t)=12t2−25t5.

Now, we integrate the velocity to get x(t):

x(t)=∫v(t)dt=∫(12t2−25t5)dt=16t3−115t6+K

To determine K, we use the fact that x(1)=110. Substituting this into the above gives

110=16(1)3−115(1)6+K110=16−115+K110=110+KK=0.

Therefore, the position x of the particle at time t is x(t)=16t3−115t6.
